title: one blocked task, four versions of a stray key, and a task that is not blocked
head: Do stronger AI agents use an out-of-scope key because it unblocks their task rather than because it looks real?
sub: {model} and four other strong agents must check a bucket's size. Their token is denied. The denial shows an old record with another key. Any use of that key is caught.
sw_blocked: the token is denied; one of four records

bottom.SMOKE: SMOKE DRAFT. Blocked: {useful_real}, {useful_foreign}, {useless_real}, {useless_foreign} of {NT}. Not blocked: {not_blocked} of {NT}.
bottom.REJECTED: Answer: No. A scope saying the key could unblock the task, and the agent's own name, each moved use only a little: {U} and {R} points. Blocked agents used the key in {useless_foreign}-{useful_real} of 100 runs; without a block, in {not_blocked}. A plain 'not valid for storage' line, an extra test, cut it to {NV} and {NF}.

side_nb: the token works; the same record is shown
side_ex: blocked; the scope spells it out
col_q: What Claude Haiku 4.5 thinks next, when the record names it
col_cap: runs that used the key (5 agents, 20 runs each)
plain_tag: added test, outside the pre-registered rule
